Subject: RE: Unit economics deep-dive & pricing qualification (FintechX) — analysis attached

Thanks, James — this is exactly what we needed. Attached is a short unit-economics note and our recommended pilot pricing (see Redwood_pricing_grid_v3.pdf). Key highlights from our analysis (assumes $50 / 1M tokens baseline):

Unit-econ summary (illustrative):
- Chat completions (avg 680 tokens per request): 680 / 1,000,000 * $50 = $0.034 / chat request. At 1M monthly chat requests this is $34k monthly inference cost.
- Embeddings (batched avg 1,000 tokens per batch of 10 docs -> 100 tokens/doc equivalent): net cost per embed-call (batch) ~ $0.05.
- Reranking/batch scoring (avg 2,000 tokens / job): 2,000 / 1,000,000 * $50 = $0.10 / job.

$/feature -> business impact (example):
- If average revenue per MAU is $3.50/month and average chats per MAU is 4, then incremental gross margin contribution per MAU needs to cover inference cost + hosting. With the numbers above, inference cost per MAU (4 chats) = 4 * $0.034 = $0.136 / MAU.
- CAC payback sensitivity: you mentioned CAC ~ $30–$50. At ARPU $3.50/mo and incremental gross margin after inference & infra of ~$2.50/mo, payback is ~12–20 months. Reducing inference unit cost by 20% improves payback materially (~2–4 months).

Recommendations / next steps:
1) Pilot pricing: 3-month pilot at $48 / 1M tokens with a 20% overage discount to start (gives FintechX runway to validate growth). Requires a 3-month minimum commit.
2) Reserved option: 6–12mo committed capacity at $42–45 / 1M tokens with throughput SLAs and burst capacity for spiky traffic.
3) Technical: Aditya will scope caching/batching opportunities — early wins typically reduce effective token consumption ~10–25% depending on session stickiness.
4) Compliance: we’ll send the SOC2 and procurement packet + standard SOW template.

Attachments: Redwood_pricing_grid_v3.pdf (pricing options), unit-econ-calcs (spreadsheet snippet embedded).

If that looks reasonable I can put together an SOW + pilot proposal for review. Would you prefer we model the conservative 120–150M token case or the aggressive 200M+ case for committed pricing?
